Used 5 views so far. 3 remaining. Let me check Gray_Mold stem and Alternaria to cover more classes.
Used 7 views (including test image). 1 remaining. Let me check Rhizopus pod for the macroscopic appearance.

## Analysis

**Test image**: Tomato stem with white cottony mycelium, many small black dots (sclerotia/sporangia) scattered on the white fungal growth, bleached/dried stem tissue to the right. Stem-affected disease.

**Reference comparison summary**:
- **Southern_Blight/stem**: White bleached area on stem, but the reference didn't show clear sclerotia
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot/stem (Bugwood_21)**: White bleached stem near soil line with a few dark sclerotia — fairly similar. Bugwood_4 showed larger rice-grain sclerotia inside split stem tissue
- **Rhizopus/stem**: Microscopic view, not comparable macroscopically; pod image showed watery soft rot — no match
- **Gray_Mold/stem**: Brown/tan canker — no match
- **Alternaria/stem**: Dark canker at soil line — no match

**Decision**: The test image shows white cottony mycelium on the stem with many small black round bodies scattered throughout. Southern Blight (Sclerotium rolfsii) produces exactly this — white mycelial mats at the stem base with numerous small spherical sclerotia that darken from white/tan to black. The sclerotia in the test image are small and numerous (mustard-seed scale), which fits Southern Blight better than Sclerotinia (which has fewer, larger, rice-grain sclerotia). The Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot stem references showed fewer and larger sclerotia.
